exercise.name: Band Close Grip Biceps Curl

reference.title: Band Close Grip Biceps Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

equipment: Resistance band (two, or one long band under both feet)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl up, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower lowering, a wider stance on the band, then the next band up.

cues.text: Stand on the bands with the feet close together, knees soft. A band end in each hand in front of the thighs, hands close together (narrower than the hips), palms forward, elbows by the sides.
Breathe out and curl the hands up toward the chest, keeping the elbows at the sides and the hands close.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, where the band is most stretched; elbows still by the sides.
Breathe in and lower against the band to straight arms.
Short pause with the arms straight and the band taut, then curl again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows drifting forward or flaring out
mistakes.fix: Pin the elbows to the sides of the ribs.
Stand tall, knees soft; use a lighter band.
Keep the hands close, narrower than the hips.

kinematics.norm: Nearly straight to about 130 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Palms forward (supinated); a supinated grip gives the highest biceps activity among curl grips (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018).
Upper arms stay beside the trunk, drifting forward only a little at the top (clinical opinion)
Hands narrower than the hips (clinical opinion)
Each band under the ball of its own foot; tension rises toward the top. Elastic resistance can match free weights (Andersen 2010).
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Close Grip Biceps Curl, video (movement reference)
Coratella et al. 2023, biceps brachii and brachioradialis excitation in biceps curl exercise: different handgrips, different synergy (Sports 11(3):64; PMC10054060)
Marcolin et al. 2018, differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl (PeerJ 6:e5165; PMC6047503)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Keep the bands securely under the feet; a band that slips can whip up toward the face.
Elbow or wrist pain with the close grip: widen the hands to shoulder width (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
progressions: Stronger band or a wider stance on the band.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main mover: bends the elbow and keeps the forearm turned palm-up; the supinated grip gives the highest biceps activity (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main mover: bends the elbow and keeps the forearm turned palm-up; the supinated grip gives the highest biceps activity (Coratella 2023; Marcolin 2018).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the band and assist elbow flexion (brachioradialis).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the band and assist elbow flexion (brachioradialis).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm still as the band pulls the hand down.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the upper arm still as the band pulls the hand down.

guides.label: Elbows bent about 130 at the top
